source_claims.statement: Maglev deoptimization reused mutable HeapNumber as immutable literal (maglev-code-generator.cc, translated-state.cc), violating V8 invariant.
Blink ImageDecoder combined cached geometry from one WebP frame with bytes from another, enabling TOCTOU heap overflow.
Crashpad ReadUpTo assumed stable memory of suspended renderer; freeze-exempt thread altered protections causing overflow.

Chain built in six days (Aug 2–7). Work split into parallel campaigns: broad search, V8 memory corruption, V8 sandbox escape, renderer sandbox escape, integration. Modular stages with clean interfaces and backup routes.

First version of chain used Gin vulnerability for V8 sandbox escape; it was a duplicate of issue 542670566. Replaced with animated WebP stage after stressful few hours. Modularity designed to guard against collisions.

research_questions.formulation: Which V8/Blink/Crashpad invariants can be violated to obtain progressive escapes from a JS context to native code execution?

unobserved_history: Exact chronological order of discovery of Maglev vs WebP vs Crashpad within the six days

forbidden_inferences: Do not assign Maglev/WebP/Crashpad to specific calendar days; article reports only the six-day total and parallel campaigns, not a day-by-day diary
